absent: Core register identifier to offset and address mapping helpers and register file layout beyond bounds checks.
Architectural vector register identifier to region decoding and vector length conversion helpers and host maximum discovery.
Counter offset ioctl payload semantics and preferred target structure beyond generic identifier.
Current cache size value source, minimum line size derivation, and selector limit definition.
System register descriptor table contents, identifier encoding helpers, visibility rules beyond write ignore, and custom setter contracts.
SMCCC filter enforcement at call time, reserved range endpoints, action meanings, and range overlap handling.
Interrupt controller range validation details and stored base address consumption.
MTE tag copy helpers, granule counts, page tagging primitives, and release path distinctions.

findings.text: Firmware register writer is available to other files for PSCI version selection, architecture workaround level selection, and feature bitmap selection, rejecting unknown selectors and wrong element widths.

System register user write path is available to other files, covering demultiplexed cache selectors and table driven system registers, with hidden registers reported as missing and designated write ignore registers accepted silently.
Virtual machine level services are available to other files for MTE tag transfer, feature identifier writable mask query, and legacy interrupt controller base address programming.
VCPU finalization and SMCCC control query and update are available to other files, with finalization limited to the vector extension feature and SMCCC control limited to the filter attribute.

Virtual machine ioctl dispatch accepts irqchip creation, device address programming, preferred target query, MTE tag copy, counter offset programming, device attribute query and update, and writable mask query, gated by protected mode policy, and rejects other requests.
VCPU ioctl entry unconditionally reports unsupported operation and dirty log synchronization entry has no observable effect in these fragments.
Device attribute query and update only support the SMCCC control group and within it only the filter attribute, with all other groups or attributes reported as unsupported.

Core register writes are confined to the core register file extent and to a bounded element size. Processor state writes are constrained by 32 bit EL0 support, 32 bit EL1 state, and nested virtualization support according to target mode class, with unrecognized modes rejected. When resulting state is 32 bit, general registers and program counter are narrowed to 32 bits, with fewer affected in user like modes than in privileged modes.

Vector length set selection is accepted only when the vector extension is present, finalization has not yet occurred, and no vector state has been allocated. The requested set must be nonempty, its maximum must not exceed the host maximum, and membership up to that maximum must exactly match host availability. On success only the maximum length is retained for later allocation.

Vector register writes distinguish the vector length set pseudo selector from architectural vector selectors. The pseudo selector is handled before finalization while architectural selectors require prior finalization and valid region decoding, with payload copied into vector storage at the decoded offset and length.
PSCI version selection is consistent with the 0.2 feature flag: legacy 0.1 is accepted only without that flag and newer versions only with it, and the accepted version is stored per virtual machine.

Architecture workaround level registers only accept values within the level mask and not above the kernel supported level. The second workaround additionally constrains its enable bit to the available level and canonicalizes four incoming availability states into two internal states, with downgrade allowed in only one direction relative to the kernel level.

Firmware feature bitmaps only accept bits within the per selector supported set. After the virtual machine has run, a bitmap write succeeds only when the value is unchanged; otherwise it reports busy.

Demultiplexed cache size writes require a clean encoding without unknown bits, a four byte element width, and an index within the selector limit. Only the cache size selector is supported; other demultiplexed selectors are reported as missing.

Cache size values must have no reserved bits set and must encode a line size at least the minimum for the instruction or data side. Identical writes without allocated override storage succeed without allocation; divergent writes lazily allocate per selector override storage initialized from current values before storing the new value.

Table driven system register writes resolve the identifier through the supplied descriptor table and treat missing or hidden entries as unknown. Entries marked user write ignore succeed without state change; entries with a custom user setter use it, otherwise the value is assigned directly to the indexed system register slot.

Vector finalization is accepted only for the vector feature when the extension is present and not already finalized. The retained maximum length must be valid and within virtualizable and architectural limits. Success allocates zeroed state sized for that length, shares it with the hypervisor, installs it on the VCPU, and marks finalized.

Legacy interrupt controller address programming applies only to the version 2 device family when that controller is present. Distributor and CPU interface addresses are validated for range overlap and alignment before being stored, with model mismatch reported as unknown device and unknown address kinds rejected.

SMCCC filter entries require zero padding, a nonzero function count without address wrap, and an action within the supported set. The first configuration installs reserved architecture ranges as hypervisor handled before inserting the requested range. Configuration after the virtual machine has run is rejected as busy.

MTE tag transfer requires MTE support, zero reserved fields, no unknown flags, page aligned address and length, and a length representable in the signed return value. Writes are rejected as busy while dirty logging is active.

MTE tag transfer proceeds one page at a time with per page resolution and online checks that reject device memory. Reads from untagged storage return zeros while reads from tagged storage copy tags out. Writes attempt tagging, copy tags in, clear tags on user access shortfall, and mark tagged. Partial progress is reported as bytes completed rather than an error code.

Writable mask query supports only the feature identifier range selector with zero reserved area, clears the caller array, then publishes masks only for feature identifier registers that are user writable and have a nonzero mask, skipping 32 bit identifier registers when 32 bit EL0 is unsupported.

Firmware bitmap updates, SMCCC filter updates, and legacy interrupt controller address updates are serialized by the per VM configuration lock, with run once and emptiness checks performed while holding it.
Irqchip creation is serialized by the per VM main lock and MTE tag transfer is serialized by the memory slot lock held across the whole page loop, including dirty logging checks and page resolution.

One register requests carry an identifier that encodes size and target class plus a user address for the payload. Firmware and system register paths derive payload width from the identifier and treat width mismatch or unresolvable targets as missing.

SMCCC filter descriptors carry a base function number, a function count defining an inclusive range, an action selector, and padding that must be zero. MTE copy descriptors carry a guest address, a byte length, a user tag buffer, direction flags, and reserved fields that must be zero.

Mask range descriptors carry a range selector that must select the feature identifier range, a reserved area that must be zero, and a user array sized for that range. Device address descriptors carry a composite identifier encoding device family and address kind plus an address. Device attribute descriptors carry group, attribute, and user address.

Vector state moves from unfinalized with selectable lengths, to finalized with allocated storage, to writable architectural registers. Length selection is only possible before finalization and architectural writes only after, with finalization being one way.

Firmware bitmaps and SMCCC filters are mutable before first run and effectively immutable after: identical bitmap rewrites remain allowed while any other change reports busy, and filter inserts are refused once running. Empty filter state first transitions through reserved range installation.

Per VCPU cache size override storage moves from absent to present on first divergent write, initialized from current values for all selectors, after which indexed updates are retained. Processor state mode moves only within the envelope allowed by 32 bit support and nested virtualization enablement.

All user memory interactions can fail and are reported as access faults without partial state update except for MTE tag transfer which reports completed bytes. Payload widths are validated before copying and padding and reserved areas are validated after copying.

Cache size override allocation and vector state allocation can fail for lack of memory. Hypervisor sharing failure during vector finalization releases the freshly allocated buffer and leaves finalization unmarked.

Concurrent reconfiguration races first run: firmware bitmap and SMCCC filter writers must observe run once state under lock and report busy, and MTE writes must observe dirty logging state under lock and report busy, rather than silently changing guest visible behavior.

ABI facts: a dedicated vector length set pseudo selector exists apart from architectural vector selectors; firmware selectors exist for PSCI version, three architecture workarounds with level mask plus enable and availability encodings, and four feature bitmaps for standard, standard hypervisor, and vendor hypervisor ranges.

ABI facts: demultiplexed cache size selection uses architecture, size, coprocessor, identifier and value masks with a four byte width and bounded index; VM ioctls and SMCCC control group with filter attribute exist; legacy controller uses distributor and CPU kinds with fixed sizes; MTE uses a from guest flag; mask query uses a feature range with indexed slots derived from system register encoding fields.
